title: Demand & supply
examples: What causes the entire demand curve to move?
How does a change in consumer income affect the market?
Can you show me an example of a surplus in a market?

explain.say: Today we are learning about demand and supply in a market.
A determinant is something that shifts the whole curve.
A movement happens only because the product's own price changes.
When supply increases, the price usually goes down.
Equilibrium is where the amount buyers want equals sellers want.
Think about apples at a fruit stall in the morning.

faq.q: What is the difference between a shift and a movement?
faq.a: A movement happens only because the product's own price changes. A shift happens because of something else, like income or tastes.
asks: Does price change cause a shift?
When is it a shift versus a movement?

faq.q: What causes a surplus in the market?
faq.a: A surplus happens when the quantity supplied is greater than the quantity demanded. This usually pushes the price down.
asks: Why would prices drop if too much is sold?
What happens when supply is too high?

faq.q: How does a decrease in income affect the market?
faq.a: If a product is a normal good, a decrease in income will decrease the demand, shifting the curve left.
asks: Does income affect all goods the same way?
What if the good is a necessity?

faq.a: The equilibrium point is the price and quantity where the market clears. At this point, supply perfectly matches demand.
asks: How do I find the market balance?
What does it mean for supply and demand to meet?

faq.q: Can a change in tastes affect the price?
faq.a: No, a change in tastes shifts the entire demand curve. It does not cause a movement along the existing curve.
asks: Is a trend change a shift or a movement?
Does fashion change affect the equilibrium?

facts: Determinants are factors other than the product's own price.
A movement along the curve is caused only by a change in the good's own price.
If demand increases, the equilibrium price will rise, assuming supply stays constant.
If supply decreases, the equilibrium price will rise, assuming demand stays constant.

quiz.say: If consumer tastes suddenly favor electric cars, what happens to the market for electric cars?

options.show: The demand curve shifts right, but the price stays the same.
options.say: The demand curve shifts right, but the price stays the same.

options.show: There is a movement up the demand curve.
options.say: There is a movement up the demand curve.

options.show: The demand curve shifts right, increasing equilibrium price and quantity.
options.say: The demand curve shifts right, increasing equilibrium price and quantity.

quiz.why: A change in tastes is a determinant, which shifts the entire demand curve outwards.

wrong.0: A shift in demand must change the equilibrium price unless supply also shifts.
wrong.1: A movement is only caused by the product's own price changing, not by tastes.
wrong.3: This confuses the cause with the effect on supply.

quiz.say: If the cost of raw materials for bread increases, what happens to the bread market?

options.show: The supply curve shifts left, increasing equilibrium price and decreasing quanti
options.say: The supply curve shifts left, increasing equilibrium price and decreasing quanti

options.show: There is a movement down the supply curve.
options.say: There is a movement down the supply curve.

quiz.why: Increased costs reduce profitability, causing suppliers to offer less at every price.

wrong.1: The cost of materials affects production (supply), not consumer desire (demand).
wrong.2: A movement implies the price changed, but the cost change affects the entire supply relationship.
wrong.3: A decrease in supply due to higher costs must lead to a higher equilibrium price.

quiz.say: If the price of coffee rises, what happens to the demand for tea (a substitute)?

options.show: The demand curve for tea shifts right, increasing equilibrium price and quantity
options.say: The demand curve for tea shifts right, increasing equilibrium price and quantity

options.show: The demand curve for tea shifts left.
options.say: The demand curve for tea shifts left.

options.show: There is a movement up the tea demand curve.
options.say: There is a movement up the tea demand curve.

options.show: The equilibrium price for tea remains unchanged.
options.say: The equilibrium price for tea remains unchanged.

quiz.why: Since coffee and tea are substitutes, a higher price for coffee makes people switch to tea.

wrong.1: Substitutes are goods people switch to when one becomes too expensive.
wrong.2: The price change of a different good (coffee) causes a shift, not a movement.
wrong.3: A change in the price of a related good will definitely change the market equilibrium.
